newsitem.title: UK: Powergen, Siemens in gas turbine tech deal.
newsitem.headline: Powergen, Siemens in gas turbine tech deal.

text.p: British electricity generator PowerGen Plc said on Wednesday it had signed an agreement with German industrial giant Siemens to build and operate a 150 million pound ($245.3 million) gas turbine technology centre in the UK.

PowerGen said in a statement the project would entail construction of the centre at its Cottam power station in central England with capacity of 500 megaWatts and that it would sell electricity generated at the site.
Work on the project will start in May and will create up to 500 construction jobs. When completed the centre will employ up to 50 staff.

The plant is expected to come onstream in the spring of 1999 and will primarily be used for testing and demonstration of the latest gas turbine technology in a commercial combined cycle power plant. It will have the capacity for prolonged demonstation runs rather than brief test-bed trials.

The joint venture follows full planning clearance for the project, including agreement from Britain's Department of Trade and Industry to build a new 24-kilometre gas pipeline from Cottam to the national gas transmission system at Blyborough, Lincolnshire in eastern England.
The project will be run by a joint venture company -- Cottam Development Centre Ltd -- and investment will be shared equally between PowerGen and Siemens.
PowerGen group managing director Deryk King said, "The Cottam Development Centre is an innovative project which marries the expertise of both companies to move the industry forward."
